title: Queue-row draw predicate lacks the count pass's amber_pct>0 guard — amber=0 breaks the row-for-row measure/draw contract
evidence: Count pass (noc_queue_rows, :602): `if p.q[0] + p.q[1] + p.q[2] > 0 || (amber_pct > 0 && p.util_pct >= u32(amber_pct)) {` — amber 0 disables the util branch. Draw pass (:772): `if p.q[0] + p.q[1] + p.q[2] == 0 && p.util_pct < u32(amber_pct) {` — with amber 0, `util_pct < u32(0)` is never true, so NO pipe is skipped: every pipe draws a queue row the measure pass never counted. The red pipes draw pass has the symmetric guard (:833): `if cat.balance.warnings.pipe_red_pct <= 0 || p.util_pct < u32(cat.balance.warnings.pipe_red_pct) {`. The r2 test pins the amber-0 semantics the draw violates: `testing.expect_value(t, noc_queue_rows(&sr, 0), i32(1))  // amber 0 = only the queued pipe`. Contract (:570): `// MUST agree with draw_noc_panel row-for-row (same count predicates + the`.
detail: The r2 N4 fix parameterized both predicates but only the count side guards amber_pct>0. With catalog pipe_amber_pct=0 (a semantic the new test authors and pins), draw renders a queue row per pipe while the scroll-clamp measure counts only queued pipes — sections misalign/overdraw.
recommended_fix: Mirror the count guard in the draw skip: `if p.q[0]+p.q[1]+p.q[2] == 0 && (amber_pct <= 0 || p.util_pct < u32(amber_pct)) { continue }` — same shape as the red pipes pass at :833.
